references.text: Israel is called a holy people and the Lord's treasured possession (סְגֻלָּה), the same term used in Exodus 19:5 regarding Israel's special standing among the nations.
Reiterates the concept of Israel as a holy people and a treasured possession (סְגֻלָּה) that the Lord has chosen from all peoples on earth.
The Lord confirms that Israel shall be his treasured possession (סְגֻלָּה), as he has promised, linked to obedience to his commands.
Confirms that the earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord, supporting the statement 'for the whole earth is mine' in Exodus 19:5.
God declares that the world and all it contains belong to him, paralleling the claim of God's ownership over the entire earth.
Describes Israel as the people God has formed for himself, connecting to the idea of Israel as God's treasured possession.
Uses the term סְגֻלָּה for those who fear the Lord and promises that they will be his own on the day he acts.
Christ gave himself to cleanse a people belonging to him (λαὸν περιούσιον), reflecting the concept of the treasured possession from Exodus 19:5.
Believers are called a chosen race, a royal priesthood, and a people for God's own possession (λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν), applying the covenant promises to the church.
The people promise to obey all that the Lord has said, and the covenant is confirmed with blood—the fulfillment of the condition to hear the Lord's voice and keep his covenant.
A direct theological parallel showing how the condition for being God's special possession (Ex 19) is expressed as sovereignty over nations (Dt 28).
Highlights the connection between Israel's status as a 'precious possession' and God's loving protection based on that same value.
Prophetic fulfillment showing how 'being God's people' (Ex 19) is restored and realized in the new covenant (Ezekiel).
